why: A whole Zoho Books export, held as JSON strings rather than TypeScript template literals ON PURPOSE: a literal CRLF inside a template literal is at the mercy of the editor, of prettier and of git's autocrlf, so the fixture that exists to prove CRLF handling would be the first thing silently rewritten to LF -- and it would still pass. JSON's escapes survive all three. Every date here is in 2026 or 2027, so no value can coincide with the real clock. AND THE ORDERS DISAGREE WITH THE ANSWERS: Invoice.csv interleaves a three-line invoice with a two-line one and introduces the LATER-dated, HIGHER-numbered document first, so an importer that assumed rows were contiguous, or that sorted on the way through, would disagree with the expected output. Contacts.csv does the same with two contact-person rows per firm.

datesDisagree.why: Every day in this file is 12 or lower, so DD/MM and MM/DD both read every value and they DISAGREE about which day each one is. Nothing may be imported: 05/06/2027 is the 5th of June or the 6th of May, both are real days, and no report drawn afterwards could ever show which was meant.
